exams.name: National Board of Podiatry Examiners examinations
exams.notes: Applicant must have passed examinations administered by the national board of podiatry examiners; no applicant shall be licensed who has not received a passing score on all board-approved examinations.
exams.quote: An applicant for licensure by examination shall submit evidence to the board that the applicant has passed the examinations administered by the national board of podiatry examiners for students graduating from colleges of podiatry

exams.name: Clinical and written examinations (board-determined)
exams.notes: Subjects determined by the board and taken from subjects taught in accredited colleges of podiatric medicine.
exams.quote: shall furnish the board an official transcript and take clinical and written examinations as the board deems necessary

interval_years.quote: All licensees shall renew their licenses on or before January 1 of every second year.

required.quote: As a condition of renewal, all applicants shall furnish the board with evidence of completion of postgraduate study as required by board rule.

available.quote: An applicant for expedited licensure by reciprocity shall meet the qualifications set forth in Section 61-8-8 NMSA 1978, shall file an application under oath on forms supplied by the board that conform to board rules on reciprocity and furnish proof satisfactory to the board of having been licensed by national examination in another licensing jurisdiction.

requirements.value: Must meet qualifications of Section 61-8-8; file application under oath; furnish proof of valid, unrestricted license; have practiced podiatry for at least three consecutive years immediately preceding filing; be in good standing with the other licensing jurisdiction; pay required fees.
requirements.quote: furnish the board an affidavit from the applicant's state board showing a valid, unrestricted license and the fact that the applicant has been licensed to practice podiatry and has practiced podiatry for at least three consecutive years immediately preceding the filing of the application for reciprocal licensure and is in good standing with the other licensing jurisdiction
